description: Brainstorm with the user: define something unclear, or generate new ideas — via problem structuring (MECE, pyramid, problem trees), ideation, idea sparring, pre-mortem, first-principles audit, or six thinking hats. Intent test: use whenever the user's subject is vague, undefined, or unstructured and they want to pin it down, or they want options that do not exist yet — even when they never say 'brainstorm'. Also on any mode-specific ask: 'structure this problem', 'give me ideas', 'spar this idea', 'pre-mortem this', 'what could go wrong', 'first-principles this', 'six hats'. NOT for something the user already holds clearly and wants understood or aligned on — that is `interview`.

Hand work over to a future agent with zero context: transfer ALL session knowledge about the handed-off work into one complete, cold-startable document. Use when the user says 'handoff', 'hand over', 'hand this off', 'prepare this for another agent', 'save where we are', 'another session will continue this' — and whenever work is about to leave this session unfinished for someone else to resume, even when no handoff word appears. Do NOT write the document from instinct: this skill carries the completeness standard a zero-context agent needs to resume.

Interview the user with hard, critical questions to excavate and pressure-test their thinking on an idea, plan, or problem. Use when the user says 'interview me', 'grill me', 'question me', 'ask me questions about', 'pressure-test my thinking', 'poke holes in this' — and whenever the job is to extract something already formed in the user's head, even when they never say 'interview'. Do NOT improvise the questioning: this skill carries the question protocol (rounds, question count, challenge standard). Intent test: the subject is already CLEAR in the user's head and the job is to understand and align on it — where it is still unclear and needs defining, or the user wants new ideas, use `brainstorm` instead.

Investignosis — investigate and/or diagnose something in the code or file base, in two consecutive passes: investigate gathers and reports evidence and stops BEFORE naming a cause; diagnose then lands on a defended root cause. Use when the user says 'investigate', 'diagnose', 'debug', 'root cause', 'figure out why', 'look into', 'why is X happening' — and on ANY request that requires reading multiple files or discovering which files to read, even when no investigation word appears. Do NOT start searching from instinct: the pass structure is what keeps evidence separate from verdict and makes the diagnosis defensible.

Owner-ruled triage of a backlog file — a `{name}-tasks.md` task file, a run/goal-folder `issues.md`, or a `loose-ends.md`. Separates entries with real present value from hygiene/speculation, gets owner rulings, then applies them in place. Use when the user says 'triage', 'clean up', 'prune', 'go through the backlog', 're-prioritize', or complains a backlog is bloated with agent-generated entries — even when they never say 'triage'. Do NOT prune by your own judgment: this skill carries the value bar and the owner-ruling protocol.
